headline: Fruit is bribery—tasty packages that convince animals to spread seeds
universal_truth: Getting others to help often requires giving them something they want
fun_facts: Many fruits are designed to pass through animal digestive systems—seeds germinate better after being eaten
Some fruits evolved to be eaten by dinosaurs; after extinction, new animals took over seed-spreading duties
The avocado was likely spread by giant ground sloths; today humans are its main dispersers
discussion_questions: Why would a plant 'want' its seeds eaten?
What happens to a fruit after an animal eats it?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Why do apples taste good? Not for you—for the tree. Fruit is a bribe: 'Eat me, carry my seeds somewhere else.' The sweetness is payment for transportation. Plants can't walk, so they recruit animals to move their offspring.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Being eaten seems like a bad strategy for survival. Why would plants wrap their seeds in something delicious that gets consumed?
cliff.prompt: Why do plants make tasty fruit around their seeds?

options.text: Animals eat the fruit, travel somewhere, and deposit seeds in their droppings—free transportation and fertilizer
options.response: Yes. The seed survives digestion, travels with the animal, and gets deposited with ready-made fertilizer. It's a transportation deal.

options.text: The sweet fruit protects seeds from rotting before they can grow
options.response: Protection helps, but the main purpose is convincing animals to carry seeds away...

q1.title: Seed Taxis
q1.script: A seed falling beneath its parent competes with that parent. Plants benefit when seeds travel far. Fruit recruits animal taxis—birds, mammals, even fish—to carry seeds miles from home. Distance equals opportunity.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Seed Taxis"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Digestive Benefits
q2.script: Many seeds germinate better after passing through digestive systems. Stomach acid weakens the seed coat. Droppings provide fertilizer. Being eaten isn't just tolerated—it's often beneficial to the seed.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Lost Partners
q3.script: The avocado evolved to be eaten by giant ground sloths—now extinct. Its large seed was meant for large digesters. Today, only humans regularly spread avocado seeds. We've become the substitute for prehistoric sloths.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Getting others to help often requires giving them something they want. Fruit teaches that the best partnerships are mutually beneficial. You get transported; they get fed. Everybody wins.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 146. Tomorrow, we'll explore what counts as a vegetable. Until then, when you eat fruit, remember: you're being bribed by a plant.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Mutual Benefit - Create Win-Wins
growTrack.activity: Think of a relationship where both sides benefit—a 'fruit deal' in your life. Where are you providing value to get something you need? Where might you create new mutual benefits? The best partnerships make both sides better off.
